events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $2.44 (model confidence 0.72)
events.body:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered trip, so the fare is meter-based and extra mileage directly increases the charge; the charged $40.18 comprises distance $27.23 over 19.3 km [F6], and the actual 19.3 km exceeds the optimal 17.3 km by 2.1 km [F1], billed as $2.90 excess distance [F4]. RD-1 treats each off-route segment as a deviation to be tested against RD-3/RD-4/RD-5, and there is one such segment: 21:47–21:50, 1.76 km driven against 0.03 km optimal, adding 1.73 km [F3].

RD-4 does not exempt the segment: the traffic record shows only moderate speed bands (SLE band 4, TPE band 5) and no incidents near the route [F10][F11][F12], and a speed band alone cannot exempt a segment under RD-4(b), with no qualifying incident under RD-4(a).

RD-5 is the decisive question. The driver's message came before the deviation (21:43 request, 21:44 agreement, segment at 21:47–21:50) [F7][F8][F3]. But RD-5 exempts only the route change the driver actually named: the driver named "the petrol station just ahead" — a stop immediately ahead on the way — and the rider consented to that, not to a 1.73 km excursion reaching 979 m off the optimal route [F7][F8][F3]. RD-3(b) addresses rider-requested stops and does not apply here, because this was a driver-proposed route change [F3][F7]; the consent therefore does not stretch to the unnamed lateral excursion. The driver's own statement confirms he treated the rider's "short stop" consent as licence for "a small change of route" [F9], which is exactly the stretched reading RD-5 forecloses. The segment is therefore not exempt.

Because the segment is unexempt, RD-2 applies: on a RydeTAXI trip the refund is the unexempt segment's extra km × the per-km rate, where the rate is distance_fare ÷ distance_km = $27.23 ÷ 19.3 km = $1.41088.../km [F3][F6]. Refund = 1.73 km × $1.41088/km = $2.4408, rounded to $2.44 [F3][F4][F6][RD-2]. The residual between the billed $2.90 excess and the segment sums is map-matching residue not refundable under RD-2 [F4][F6]. Waiting was charged $0.00, so RD-3(c) raises no separate issue [F6].

RD-6 is not triggered: the driver's profile records 2 upheld disputes but route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so this case does not make the breach "repeated" and no account flag is added [F15][RD-6]. The rider's clean profile is noted but plays no part in the outcome [F14].

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: We reviewed your fare and found that part of your trip went off the best route without a valid reason. The driver's message mentioned a stop just ahead, but the detour actually went well off the route, so that detour isn't covered by your agreement to a short stop. Because of that, we're refunding $2.44 for the extra distance. It will be paid to you as a Ryde voucher. Nothing else changes on your account, and no action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed a route dispute on this trip. Part of your route went off the best path by about 1.7 km. You messaged the rider about stopping at a petrol station just ahead, but the detour went much further off route than that stop, so it isn't covered by the rider's consent. We're recording a route breach on your file. No account flag is being added, since this doesn't count as repeated route issues on your record. $2.44 of the fare is being refunded to the rider as a Ryde voucher, which Ryde covers — so nothing is deducted from your earnings for this trip.
